pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What word describes manure made from once-living things? (1 mark)
   A. Metal
   B. Plastic
   C. Organic
   D. Mineral only

2. What is the meaning of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Using as much as possible
   B. Storing dirty water
   C. Using it carefully so none is wasted
   D. Selling water

3. Where should kerosene be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a water bottle on the table
   B. In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   C. In an open bowl
   D. Near the fire

4. What is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A type of soil
   C. A cleaning tool
   D. Something we burn to get heat

5. What is biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Only wild plants
   B. Only birds
   C. A type of crop
   D. The variety of living things on Earth

6. Why is poison a bad way to deal with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. It makes crops grow
   B. It is too slow to spread
   C. It is too cheap
   D. It can also kill other animals and people

7. Why do some farmers tie a young tree to a stake? (1 mark)
   A. To stop it growing
   B. To feed it
   C. To keep it upright in wind
   D. To make it thicker

8. What is a fruit? (1 mark)
   A. The leaves of a plant
   B. The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   C. The roots of a plant
   D. The stem of a plant

9. Why should young fruit trees be watered in dry weather? (1 mark)
   A. Water kills them
   B. They do not need water
   C. Water makes fruit sour
   D. Their roots are small and cannot reach much water

10. Which nutrient in oranges and guavas helps the body to heal cuts and fight colds? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Salt
   C. Starch
   D. Vitamin C

11. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Hold the tree and take in water and food
   B. Make fruits
   C. Produce seeds
   D. Collect sunlight

12. Why should a poultry house be clean and dry? (1 mark)
   A. To stop hens from laying
   B. To keep birds healthy and safe
   C. To attract rats
   D. To make eggs blue

13. Which of these is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Zebra
   C. Lion
   D. Giraffe

14. Which animal is not domestic? (1 mark)
   A. Cow
   B. Elephant
   C. Hen
   D. Goat

15. Which of these is an energy-giving food? (1 mark)
   A. Spinach
   B. Orange
   C. Fish
   D. Ugali

16. Which meal is missing protective foods? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato, egg and spinach
   B. Githeri and avocado
   C. Ugali, beans and cabbage
   D. Rice and fish only

17. Which food group gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Water only
   B. Energy-giving foods
   C. Salt
   D. Protective foods only

18. Which way should pot handles point? (1 mark)
   A. Inward, away from the edge
   B. Outward over the floor
   C. Towards children
   D. Down into the fire

19. Which food may be served with boiled potatoes for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Soda only
   B. Vegetable stew
   C. Sugar
   D. A second helping of potatoes only

20. What can be used if there is no soap? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Sugar
   C. Clean ash and running water
   D. Mud

21. Why should you bathe every day? (1 mark)
   A. To waste water
   B. To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   C. To make the body hot
   D. To make skin dry

22. Why should we wear shoes? (1 mark)
   A. To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   B. To be heavier
   C. To hide our feet
   D. To make us tall

23. Why should combs and towels not be shared? (1 mark)
   A. Germs and lice can spread
   B. They break
   C. They become dirty faster
   D. They are too big

24. Which waste should not be burnt because the smoke is harmful? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Wood
   D. Paper

25. Which method removes dry dirt from the floor with a broom? (1 mark)
   A. Dusting
   B. Mopping
   C. Sweeping
   D. Washing

26. Which is a correct step for cleaning gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Snatch them off by the fingers
   B. Wear them wet
   C. Put them on again dirty
   D. Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin

27. How should rubber gloves be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a fire
   B. Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   C. Leave them dirty
   D. Wash with a stone

28. Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem? (1 mark)
   A. It grows mould and smells
   B. It becomes stronger
   C. It becomes lighter
   D. It becomes cleaner

29. What is the use of labelling PPE? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. So each item goes back to its owner
   C. To hide it
   D. To tear it

30. Which PPE protects the feet from mud and water? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Gumboots
   C. Headgear
   D. Dust mask

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)

32. Describe how to plant a fruit seedling. (4 marks)

33. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

34. Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops. (4 marks)

35. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)

36. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)

37. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

38. Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe? (2 marks)

39. Give three ways of caring for a fruit crop. (3 marks)

40. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)

41. Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel. (3 marks)

42. Give three uses of goats. (3 marks)

43. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)

44. State two ways of making drinking water safe. (2 marks)

45. Explain four benefits of conserving fuel. (4 marks)

46. Name two materials that can be used to make compost. (2 marks)

47. What are tacking stitches? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Organic
   Organic means it comes from plants and animals.

2. C — Using it carefully so none is wasted
   Conserving means saving and protecting.

3. B — In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   Kerosene catches fire easily and is poisonous.

4. D — Something we burn to get heat
   Fuels such as wood and gas are burnt for heat.

5. D — The variety of living things on Earth
   Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

6. D — It can also kill other animals and people
   Poison harms living things that are not the target.

7. C — To keep it upright in wind
   Stakes protect against bending.

8. B — The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

9. D — Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   Young trees are easily stressed by drought.

10. D — Vitamin C
   Vitamin C helps the body fight illness.

11. A — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

12. B — To keep birds healthy and safe
   Dirty houses spread diseases.

13. A — Goat
   Goats are kept by farmers.

14. B — Elephant
   Elephants are wild.

15. D — Ugali
   Ugali is a starchy staple.

16. D — Rice and fish only
   Rice and fish have energy and protein but no vegetables or fruits.

17. B — Energy-giving foods
   Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

18. A — Inward, away from the edge
   Handles sticking out can be knocked.

19. B — Vegetable stew
   Vegetables add protective foods.

20. C — Clean ash and running water
   Ash helps to remove dirt when soap is not available.

21. B — To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   Bathing keeps the body clean.

22. A — To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   Shoes protect the feet.

23. A — Germs and lice can spread
   Personal items should be for one person.

24. A — Plastic
   Burning plastics gives harmful smoke.

25. C — Sweeping
   Sweeping uses a broom.

26. D — Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin
   This prevents germs touching the skin.

27. B — Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

28. A — It grows mould and smells
   Moulds grow in damp places.

29. B — So each item goes back to its owner
   Labels avoid mix-ups.

30. B — Gumboots
   Gumboots are waterproof.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watering, weeding, mulching, adding compost, pruning, protecting from animals (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Large, loose temporary stitches used to hold cloth in place before permanent sewing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for temporary, 1 mark for holding cloth.
